overview.description: Durak Perevodnoy (Transfer Fool) is a fast-paced and highly tactical variation of the classic Russian shedding game Durak. While it retains the core 'attack-defense' mechanics of Podkidnoy Durak, it introduces the critical ability to 'transfer' an attack. Instead of defending, a player can play a card of the same rank as the attacker's card to shift the entire burden of defense onto the next player. This creates volatile rounds where a single card lead can grow into a massive pile of cards that moves around the table until someone is unable to defend or transfer.

history.origins: Durak emerged in the 18thndcentury Russian Empire as a game of the lower classes, but Perevodnoy (the transfer variant) gained widespread popularity in the Soviet era as a more strategic and 'fair' version that allows players to escape tough defenses.
timeline: 1800s: Basic Durak becomes Russia's most played game.
1950s: Perevodnoy variant becomes standard in urban centers like Moscow and Leningrad.
Modern: Digital versions dominate Russian app stores, with Perevodnoy often being the default competitive mode.
history.evolution: Evolution from purely defensive play to a game where 'passing the buck' is a central mechanic.
history.cultural: Played by everyone from sailors to academics; it is the ultimate 'national game' of Russia.

setup.deck: 36ndcard Russian pack (ranks 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A).
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 6 cards. The next card is placed face-up under the stock to determine the trump suit.

rules.objective: Avoid being the last player with cards in your hand.
rules.gameplay:
1. Attacking: One player leads a card to the person on their left.
2. Transferring: Instead of beating the card, the defender may play a card of the SAME RANK to 'transfer' the attack to the next player.
3. Defending: If the player cannot or will not transfer, they must beat all cards in the attack (higher rank or trump).
4. Drawing: After a round, players draw from the stock to return to a 6ndcard hand.
keyRules: You cannot transfer an attack if the next player has fewer cards in their hand than the total number of cards now in the attack.
Once you start defending (play a beating card), you can no longer transfer.
Trump cards beat all non-trump cards regardless of rank.

strategy.basic: Keep at least one card of every rank if possible. This 'rank diversity' allows you to transfer attacks and avoid being trapped with a huge pile of cards.
strategy.intermediate: Trump Conservation: Never use trumps to beat cards if the talon (stock) is still large. It is often better to pick up a few cards early to build a strong hand for the endgame.
strategy.advanced: The Transfer Trap: If you know the player to your left is low on cards, intentionally lead a rank they can transfer, so that the player AFTER them (who might be winning) gets burdened with a massive defense.
tips: If you are the defender and cannot transfer, try to beat cards with the lowest possible rank to save your power cards.
In the endgame (no deck), counting cards of the trump suit is the difference between winning and being the fool.

list.name: Kiev variation
list.description: After beating the first card(s) of the attack, if further cards are thrown in the defender can transfer those new cards to the next player by playing equal cards. The cards that are already beaten stay beaten.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variation described in source; engine overrides to be added when variant is implemented.

list.name: Pass Card (Perevodnoy durak s proyezdnym)
list.description: If the defender holds a trump of equal rank to the first attack card, the attack can be transferred to the next player by simply showing the trump. The trump does not have to be played.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variation described in source; engine overrides to be added when variant is implemented.
Reserved for future variants; no overrides defined yet.

difficulty.easy: Never transfers; always tries to beat the highest card with their highest card.
difficulty.medium: Understands the value of 'passing the buck'; saves matching ranks for defense.
difficulty.hard: Simulates potential transfers to ensure they don't accidentally trap themselves with a 6-card pick-up late in the game.

considerations: AI must calculate the hand sizes of all players to know when a transfer is legally 'blocked'.

engine.deckDescription: A stripped French deck containing 36 cards with four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades) and nine ranks per suit (6 through Ace), created by removing cards 2 through 5 from a standard 52-card deck.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card design and distinct color coding for easy suit identification.
engine.rankDescription: Nine ranks per suit starting from 6: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack (Valet), Queen (Dame), King (Roi), and Ace as the highest card, where each rank has specific value and importance in determining game outcomes.
